title: Quota Reshaping and Graceful Priority Revocation — Spec + Runbook
author: Aisha K. Patel
body:
Summary

This document specifies the Quota Reshaping and Graceful Priority Revocation feature for the Redwood serving runtime scheduler. The goal is to allow the scheduler to rebalance per-tenant and per-route resource allocations under sustained pressure without causing sharp fidelity drops, SLO violations, or oscillatory eviction behavior. The doc contains: design intent, scheduling state machine, metrics & instrumentation, operational runbook for incidents, config examples, rollout checklist, and ownership.

Why this exists

- Problem: sudden quota exhaustion, tenant burst consolidation, or hardware degradation can force hard evictions that break KV cache consistency, invalidate warmstart assumptions, and produce large P95/P99 latency regressions.
- Goal: implement a controlled, observable sequence to reshape quotas and softly revoke priority (i.e., gradually reduce slot weights / kernel credits), providing smooth fidelity degradation and clear recovery paths.

Design overview

1) Principle: degrade gracefully, prefer admission control and shaping over instantaneous preemptive evictions.
2) Surface: extends scheduler admission controller and kernel admission (credit) layer. Two coordinated actions: 
   - Quota Reshaping: modify per-cohort quotas (GPU slots / kernel share) based on observed usage and backlog.
   - Priority Revocation (soft): decrement per-request priority multiplier and re-evaluate kernel assignment; do not forcibly preempt running kernels unless safety thresholds exceeded.
3) Safety: hard-eviction remains a last resort behind multiple guarded checks.

Terminology

- slot: logical allocation unit for GPU kernel execution (existing).
- credit: kernel-level CPU/GPU time accounting token.
- cohort: grouping (tenant-route-model-version) used for quota accounting.
- soft-revoke: transient decrease of effective priority multiplier used by the scheduler when scoring requests.

State machine (high level)

1) Detect: Async monitor observes backlog growth, queue latency, kernel queue length, and GPU occupancy.
2) Candidate selection: pick cohorts with highest excess tail-impact score (see scoring below).
3) Reshape proposal: synthesize a target quota delta for each selected cohort. Proposal includes: delta_percent, grace_period_s, rollback_condition_expression.
4) Soft-apply: apply soft-revoke by reducing cohort priority by X% in increments (step size configurable). Track the impact for 'observation_window_s'.
5) Confirm/rollback: if P95 latency or fidelity metric regresses beyond configured tolerance, automatically rollback the change. If improvement persists and allowed budget used, commit the reshape to quota service.

Scoring and selection

Use a weighted score combining: queue_growth_rate (50%), p99_latency_increase (30%), recent_error_rate (10%), coldstart_fraction (10%). Normalise each signal and compute: score = 0.5*g + 0.3*l + 0.1*e + 0.1*c. Higher score -> higher candidate priority.

Key metrics & instrumentation (names are authoritative)

- scheduler.quota_reshaper.proposals.count (counter)
- scheduler.quota_reshaper.applied.count (counter)
- scheduler.priority_revocation.step_applied (gauge) — current step for cohort
- scheduler.priority_revocation.rollback.count (counter)
- runtime.kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge) — use when deciding safe reshaping targets
- runtime.p95_latency_ms (histogram) — per-cohort, per-route
- scheduler.backlog.size_by_cohort (gauge)
- scheduler.soft_revoke_active (gauge boolean)
- alerts: alert if scheduler.quota_reshaper.rollback.count > 3 within 30m for same cohort

Config example (YAML)

--8<-- CONFIG START
quota_reshaper:
  enabled: true
  max_concurrent_proposals: 5
  detection_window_s: 60
  observation_window_s: 120
  step_size_percent: 10      # reduce priority by 10% per step
  max_steps: 5               # at most 50% soft revoke
  min_grace_period_s: 30
  rollback_criteria:
    p95_latency_increase_pct_threshold: 15
    fidelity_regression_score_threshold: 0.08
    error_rate_absolute_threshold: 0.01
  selection_weights:
    queue_growth: 0.5
    p99_latency: 0.3
    errors: 0.1
    coldstart: 0.1
  hard_evict_thresholds:
    gpu_ooms_in_window: 1
    sustained_gpu_occupancy_pct: 98
--8<-- CONFIG END

Notes on tuning: step_size_percent and max_steps balance rapid recovery vs fidelity risk. Default values are conservative.

Kernel-level integration

- When the soft-revoke step changes, the scheduler attaches a priority_multiplier to the request descriptor that the kernel admission subsystem reads. Kernel admission then de-queues lower-scored requests first.
- The kernel must not preempt in-flight execution unless hard_evict_threshold is met. Instead, new admissions are biased away from revoked cohorts.

Rollout / Fallback strategy

1) Canary: enable in canary runtime region with max_concurrent_proposals=1 and observation_window_s=300. Monitor the following dashboards for 48h: p95 latency, kv_cache.hit_ratio, scheduler.quota_reshaper.* metrics.
2) Graduated rollout: increase traffic to canary cohorts and raise max_concurrent_proposals progressively.
3) Fallback: automated rollback if any rollback_criteria tripped. Manual rollback option for oncall via CLI: rshctl quota-reshaper rollback --cohort <id>

Operational runbook: immediate steps for incidents

Title: High tail latency suspected due to quota reshaping
Severity: Sev2
Owner: Serving-runtime oncall (primary)

1) Check dashboard: runtime.p95_latency_ms (global and per-cohort), scheduler.quota_reshaper.applied.count in last 30m.
2) If applied.count > 0 for suspect cohort: run rshctl quota-reshaper list --recent 30m to view proposals and steps.
3) Soft rollback (automated) will occur if criteria met. If automated rollback has not triggered and P95 > SLA threshold (see below), manually rollback: rshctl quota-reshaper rollback --cohort <id> --reason "oncall-rollback"
4) If rollback succeeds but latency remains high: escalate to runtime-sre and open PAGER channel. Collect traces: occtl traces query --cohort <id> --window 15m and attach to incident.
5) If system is oscillating (repeated apply->rollback loops): disable quota_reshaper globally: rshctl feature toggle quota_reshaper --off and file a follow-up investigation ticket.

SLA and thresholds

- Platform latency SLO (hosted tier): p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for text-generation endpoints under nominal load.
- Acceptance guard for changes: no single cohort should see p95 increase > 15% relative to baseline for longer than observation_window_s.

Safety considerations and edge cases

- KV cache thrash: avoid reducing priority for cohorts with kv_cache.hit_ratio > 0.70 unless backlog growth is extreme — we prefer shaping other cohorts first.
- Coldstart-heavy cohorts: coldstart_fraction used to downweight candidates to avoid punishing transient spikes.
- Multi-tenant entanglement: changes applied for one cohort must be visible to cross-tenant routing decision (so that downstream routing can reroute to fallback model variants).

Audit logs and governance

- Every proposal, step application, commit, and rollback is written to audit-service with fields: {proposal_id, cohort_id, author=system|user, delta_percent, steps_applied, timestamps, reason}.
- Retention: audit records retained 90 days by default; retention for enterprise private deployments configurable via policy.

Testing and benchmark plan

- Unit tests for scoring and selection (deterministic stubs).
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator (benchgen) produces sustained vs spiky patterns; run across hardware types and validate no more than 2% increase in cost/throughput envelope.
- Benchmark: run mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite (see benchmarking-and-perf-suite) for 1000 trial seeds to measure false-positive reshapes. Target false-positive rate < 1 per 1000 trials.

CLI & debugging commands

- rshctl quota-reshaper status --cohort <id>
- rshctl quota-reshaper explain --proposal <proposal_id>
- rshctl quota-reshaper rollback --cohort <id> [--force]
- rshctl metrics tail scheduler.priority_revocation.step_applied

Example proposal record (JSON)

--8<-- EXAMPLE START
{
  "proposal_id": "qr-20250901-77a3",
  "cohort_id": "tenant-234/route/text-gen/v2",
  "delta_percent": -20,
  "steps_planned": 2,
  "applied_steps": 1,
  "status": "observing",
  "created_by": "automated-detector",
  "created_at": "2025-09-01T12:34:00Z"
}
--8<-- EXAMPLE END

Ownership and follow-ups

- Primary owners: runtime-scheduler team (pager: runtime-scheduler-oncall)
- Secondary owners: runtime-kernel team (for kernel admission integration), runtime-observability (dashboards & alerts)
- Follow-up work: add cohort-impact simulation harness to benchgen; cross-validate reshaper decisions vs offline explainer scores.

Rollout checklist (preflight)

1) Unit tests green; integration tests pass locally
2) Canary dashboard created and shared with SRE and runtime product (links provided to stakeholders)
3) Set conservative defaults (step_size_percent=5, max_steps=2) for initial canary
4) Ensure audit logs visible in Splunk / Loki and retention confirmed
5) Coordinate release window with SRE (low-traffic period recommended)

Appendix: failure-mode examples

- Failure: reshaper reduces priority for cohort with 95% KV hit ratio -> causes cache miss storm -> increased p99 -> rollback. Action: add a KV-hit safeguard and raise coldstart/caching score weight.
- Failure: oscillation due to noisy signals -> add hysteresis: require two consecutive observation windows of improvement before commit.

If you have questions or want to run a localized experiment, ping Aisha on Slack (#runtime-scheduler) or open an RFC in the runtime-experiments board.
